# Scope and analysis status

The source data describe bookings at one resort hotel in the Algarve and one city hotel in Lisbon, Portugal. The source article presents the datasets and discusses cancellation-prediction uses; this project instead studies a continuous response, average daily rate (ADR), with an explanatory multiple linear regression. The hotel indicator therefore compares these two properties and does not support generalization to all city and resort hotels.

The working research question is: among non-cancelled bookings with positive ADR at these two properties, how is lead time associated with ADR, and does this association differ between the properties after adjustment for arrival timing, length of stay, party composition, meal plan, reserved room type, market segment, and customer type?

The model and diagnostics remain preliminary. Thirty-one positive-stay records that report zero adults, children, and babies are excluded under the group's updated cleaning rule.

# Import and reproduce the cleaned analysis data

The cleaning pipeline below first reproduces the supplied 73,004-row, 24-variable cleaned file directly from the original data and then removes the 31 records with no recorded guests, leaving 72,973 observations. No exact duplicate-looking rows are removed because distinct bookings can become identical after identifying and date-detail variables are excluded.

```{r data-import-cleaning}
candidate_paths <- c(
  file.path("data", "raw", "hotels.csv"),
  file.path("..", "data", "raw", "hotels.csv"),
  file.path("data", "hotels.csv"),
  file.path("..", "data", "hotels.csv"),
  "hotels.csv"
)
existing_paths <- candidate_paths[file.exists(candidate_paths)]

if (length(existing_paths) == 0L) {
  stop(
    "hotels.csv was not found. Place the original file in data/hotels.csv ",
    "or in the same folder as this Rmd file."
  )
}

raw_hotels <- read.csv(
  existing_paths[1L],
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE,
  check.names = FALSE
)

raw_hotels$source_row_id <- seq_len(nrow(raw_hotels))

month_number <- match(
  raw_hotels$arrival_date_month,
  month.name
)
raw_hotels$arrival_date <- as.Date(sprintf(
  "%04d-%02d-%02d",
  raw_hotels$arrival_date_year,
  month_number,
  raw_hotels$arrival_date_day_of_month
))

step_noncancelled <- raw_hotels[raw_hotels$is_canceled == 0, ]
step_positive_adr <- step_noncancelled[step_noncancelled$adr > 0, ]
step_known_country <- step_positive_adr[
  !is.na(step_positive_adr$country) &
    step_positive_adr$country != "" &
    step_positive_adr$country != "NULL",
]
step_valid_room <- step_known_country[
  step_known_country$reserved_room_type != "L",
]
analysis_rows <- step_valid_room[
  step_valid_room$distribution_channel != "Undefined",
]

step_valid_categories <- analysis_rows
analysis_rows <- step_valid_categories[
  step_valid_categories$adults +
    step_valid_categories$children +
    step_valid_categories$babies > 0,
]

analysis_rows$meal[analysis_rows$meal == "Undefined"] <- "SC"
analysis_rows$is_repeated_guest <- ifelse(
  analysis_rows$is_repeated_guest == 1,
  "Yes",
  "No"
)
analysis_rows$domestic <- ifelse(
  analysis_rows$country == "PRT",
  "Domestic",
  "International"
)

analysis_variables <- c(
  "hotel", "lead_time", "arrival_date_year", "arrival_date_month",
  "stays_in_weekend_nights", "stays_in_week_nights", "adults",
  "children", "babies", "meal", "market_segment",
  "distribution_channel", "is_repeated_guest",
  "previous_cancellations", "previous_bookings_not_canceled",
  "reserved_room_type", "booking_changes", "deposit_type",
  "days_in_waiting_list", "customer_type", "adr",
  "required_car_parking_spaces", "total_of_special_requests",
  "domestic"
)

hotels <- analysis_rows[analysis_variables]
source_row_id <- analysis_rows$source_row_id
arrival_date <- analysis_rows$arrival_date

cleaning_flow <- data.frame(
  Step = c(
    "Original records",
    "Retain non-cancelled bookings",
    "Retain positive ADR",
    "Remove country coded NULL",
    "Remove reserved room type L",
    "Remove undefined distribution channel",
    "Remove zero-recorded-guest bookings"
  ),
  Rows_remaining = c(
    nrow(raw_hotels),
    nrow(step_noncancelled),
    nrow(step_positive_adr),
    nrow(step_known_country),
    nrow(step_valid_room),
    nrow(step_valid_categories),
    nrow(analysis_rows)
  )
)

knitr::kable(cleaning_flow, align = c("l", "r"))
```

The source paper defines ADR as the sum of lodging transactions divided by the number of staying nights. `country == "NULL"` is removed because domestic/international status cannot be constructed, `Undefined` meal is combined with `SC` because both indicate no meal package in this data preparation, and two invalid/undefined categorical levels are excluded. The final rule removes records with `adults + children + babies == 0` because they do not describe a booking with a recorded guest. These choices must remain consistent with the Data Lead's data-description section.

## Audit checks

```{r data-audit}
audit_results <- data.frame(
  Check = c(
    "Rows", "Columns", "Missing values",
    "Additional copies of identical 24-field rows",
    "Rows belonging to identical 24-field groups",
    "Records with zero recorded guests after exclusion",
    "Zero-night records", "ADR at most one euro"
  ),
  Result = c(
    nrow(hotels),
    ncol(hotels),
    sum(is.na(hotels)),
    sum(duplicated(hotels)),
    sum(duplicated(hotels) | duplicated(hotels, fromLast = TRUE)),
    sum(with(
      hotels,
      stays_in_weekend_nights + stays_in_week_nights > 0 &
        adults + children + babies == 0
    )),
    sum(with(hotels, stays_in_weekend_nights + stays_in_week_nights == 0)),
    sum(hotels$adr <= 1)
  )
)

knitr::kable(audit_results, align = c("l", "r"))

stopifnot(nrow(hotels) == 72973L)
stopifnot(ncol(hotels) == 24L)
stopifnot(sum(is.na(hotels)) == 0L)
stopifnot(all(hotels$adr > 0))
```

The audit makes the zero-recorded-guest exclusion explicit. Very low ADR observations remain in the preliminary model because a separate exclusion rule has not been adopted.

# Variable coding

```{r variable-coding}
month_levels <- month.name

hotels$hotel <- factor(
  hotels$hotel,
  levels = c("City Hotel", "Resort Hotel")
)
hotels$arrival_date_year <- factor(
  hotels$arrival_date_year,
  levels = c(2015, 2016, 2017)
)
hotels$arrival_date_month <- factor(
  hotels$arrival_date_month,
  levels = month_levels
)
hotels$meal <- factor(
  hotels$meal,
  levels = c("BB", "HB", "SC", "FB")
)
hotels$reserved_room_type <- factor(
  hotels$reserved_room_type,
  levels = c("A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F", "G", "H")
)
hotels$market_segment <- factor(
  hotels$market_segment,
  levels = c(
    "Online TA", "Offline TA/TO", "Direct", "Groups",
    "Corporate", "Aviation", "Complementary"
  )
)
hotels$customer_type <- factor(
  hotels$customer_type,
  levels = c("Transient", "Transient-Party", "Contract", "Group")
)
```

The reference categories are City Hotel, 2015, January, BB, reserved room A, Online TA, and Transient customer. Arrival year is included as an adjustment variable because prices may differ across the 2015--2017 observation period.

# Preliminary multiple linear regression

The model includes eleven predictor variables and the required interaction. `lead_time * hotel` expands to the two lower-order terms and `lead_time:hotel`.

```{r model-fit}
working_formula <- adr ~
  lead_time * hotel +
  arrival_date_year +
  arrival_date_month +
  stays_in_weekend_nights +
  stays_in_week_nights +
  adults +
  children +
  meal +
  reserved_room_type +
  market_segment +
  customer_type

preliminary_model <- lm(working_formula, data = hotels)
```

## Coefficient estimates and model fit

```{r coefficient-table}
coefficient_matrix <- coef(summary(preliminary_model))
confidence_intervals <- confint(preliminary_model, level = 0.95)

coefficient_table <- data.frame(
  Term = rownames(coefficient_matrix),
  Estimate = coefficient_matrix[, "Estimate"],
  Standard_Error = coefficient_matrix[, "Std. Error"],
  Lower_95_CI = confidence_intervals[, 1],
  Upper_95_CI = confidence_intervals[, 2],
  p_value = coefficient_matrix[, "Pr(>|t|)"],
  row.names = NULL,
  check.names = FALSE
)

numeric_columns <- c(
  "Estimate", "Standard_Error", "Lower_95_CI", "Upper_95_CI"
)
coefficient_table[numeric_columns] <- lapply(
  coefficient_table[numeric_columns],
  function(x) round(x, 4)
)
coefficient_table$p_value <- format.pval(
  coefficient_table$p_value,
  digits = 4,
  eps = 0.0001
)

knitr::kable(coefficient_table, align = c("l", rep("r", 5)))
```

```{r model-fit-table}
model_summary <- summary(preliminary_model)
model_fit_table <- data.frame(
  Measure = c(
    "Observations", "Residual standard error", "R-squared",
    "Adjusted R-squared", "Model degrees of freedom",
    "Residual degrees of freedom"
  ),
  Value = c(
    format(nobs(preliminary_model), big.mark = ",", scientific = FALSE),
    sprintf("%.2f", sigma(preliminary_model)),
    sprintf("%.4f", model_summary$r.squared),
    sprintf("%.4f", model_summary$adj.r.squared),
    as.character(length(coef(preliminary_model)) - 1L),
    format(df.residual(preliminary_model), big.mark = ",", scientific = FALSE)
  )
)

knitr::kable(model_fit_table, align = c("l", "r"))
```

## Lead-time slopes by property

```{r interaction-slopes}
model_coefficients <- coef(preliminary_model)
interaction_name <- "lead_time:hotelResort Hotel"

city_lead_time_slope <- unname(model_coefficients["lead_time"])
resort_lead_time_slope <- unname(
  model_coefficients["lead_time"] + model_coefficients[interaction_name]
)

slope_table <- data.frame(
  Property = c("Lisbon City Hotel", "Algarve Resort Hotel"),
  Estimated_ADR_change_per_additional_lead_time_day = round(
    c(city_lead_time_slope, resort_lead_time_slope),
    4
  )
)

knitr::kable(slope_table, align = c("l", "r"))
```

The `lead_time` coefficient is the estimated mean ADR change for one additional lead-time day at the City Hotel, holding the adjustment variables fixed. The interaction coefficient is the Resort-minus-City difference between those slopes. The Resort Hotel slope is their sum. These estimates describe conditional associations, not causal effects.

# Regression diagnostics

```{r diagnostic-objects, include=FALSE}
fitted_values <- fitted(preliminary_model)
standardized_residuals <- rstandard(preliminary_model)
leverages <- hatvalues(preliminary_model)
```

## Mean structure, constant variance, and normality

```{r core-diagnostics, fig.width=12, fig.height=4.2, fig.cap="Core preliminary-model diagnostics: standardized residuals against fitted ADR, the residual distribution, and the normal QQ plot."}
old_par <- par(mfrow = c(1, 3), mar = c(4, 4, 3, 1))

plot(
  fitted_values, standardized_residuals,
  xlab = "Fitted ADR (euros per night)",
  ylab = "Standardized residual",
  main = "Residuals vs fitted ADR",
  pch = 16, cex = 0.3, col = rgb(0, 0, 0, 0.16)
)
abline(h = 0, col = "red", lwd = 2)

hist(
  standardized_residuals,
  breaks = 50,
  xlab = "Standardized residual",
  main = "Residual distribution",
  col = "grey85", border = "white"
)
abline(v = 0, col = "red", lwd = 2)

qqnorm(
  standardized_residuals,
  main = "Normal QQ plot",
  pch = 16, cex = 0.3, col = rgb(0, 0, 0, 0.16)
)
qqline(standardized_residuals, col = "red", lwd = 2)

par(old_par)
```

## Main predictor, hotel indicator, and leverage

```{r targeted-diagnostics, fig.width=12, fig.height=4.2, fig.cap="Targeted diagnostics for the main predictor and hotel indicator, together with standardized residuals against leverage."}
old_par <- par(mfrow = c(1, 3), mar = c(4, 4, 3, 1))

plot(
  hotels$lead_time, standardized_residuals,
  xlab = "Lead time (days)",
  ylab = "Standardized residual",
  main = "Residuals vs lead time",
  pch = 16, cex = 0.3, col = rgb(0, 0, 0, 0.16)
)
abline(h = 0, col = "red", lwd = 2)

boxplot(
  standardized_residuals ~ hotels$hotel,
  xlab = "Property", ylab = "Standardized residual",
  main = "Residuals by property"
)
abline(h = 0, col = "red", lwd = 2)

plot(
  leverages, standardized_residuals,
  xlab = "Leverage", ylab = "Standardized residual",
  main = "Residuals vs leverage",
  pch = 16, cex = 0.3, col = rgb(0, 0, 0, 0.16)
)
abline(h = 0, col = "red", lwd = 2)

par(old_par)
```

## Residuals in data order and calendar time

```{r dependence-diagnostics, fig.width=12, fig.height=4.2, fig.cap="Dependence checks using the source-row order, reconstructed arrival date, and the residual autocorrelation function in source-row order."}
old_par <- par(mfrow = c(1, 3), mar = c(4, 4, 3, 1))

plot(
  source_row_id, standardized_residuals,
  xlab = "Source row order", ylab = "Standardized residual",
  main = "Residuals in source order",
  pch = 16, cex = 0.25, col = rgb(0, 0, 0, 0.14)
)
abline(h = 0, col = "red", lwd = 2)

plot(
  arrival_date, standardized_residuals,
  xlab = "Arrival date", ylab = "Standardized residual",
  main = "Residuals over arrival dates",
  pch = 16, cex = 0.25, col = rgb(0, 0, 0, 0.14)
)
abline(h = 0, col = "red", lwd = 2)

acf(
  standardized_residuals,
  lag.max = 40,
  main = "Residual ACF in source order"
)

par(old_par)
```

## Other numerical predictors and selected factors

```{r additional-diagnostics, fig.width=12, fig.height=7.5, fig.cap="Residual checks for the remaining numerical predictors and selected categorical adjustment variables."}
old_par <- par(mfrow = c(2, 3), mar = c(6, 4, 3, 1))

numerical_predictors <- c(
  "stays_in_weekend_nights", "stays_in_week_nights", "adults", "children"
)

for (variable in numerical_predictors) {
  plot(
    hotels[[variable]], standardized_residuals,
    xlab = variable, ylab = "Standardized residual",
    main = paste("Residuals vs", variable),
    pch = 16, cex = 0.3, col = rgb(0, 0, 0, 0.16)
  )
  abline(h = 0, col = "red", lwd = 2)
}

boxplot(
  standardized_residuals ~ hotels$arrival_date_month,
  las = 2, xlab = "Arrival month", ylab = "Standardized residual",
  main = "Residuals by month"
)
abline(h = 0, col = "red", lwd = 2)

boxplot(
  standardized_residuals ~ hotels$customer_type,
  las = 2, xlab = "Customer type", ylab = "Standardized residual",
  main = "Residuals by customer type"
)
abline(h = 0, col = "red", lwd = 2)

par(old_par)
```

# Preliminary assumption assessment

| Assumption or condition | Preliminary assessment |
|---|---|
| Correct linear mean structure | Questionable. Residual-versus-fitted and residual-versus-lead-time plots show systematic structure; the large change in spread also makes the mean pattern harder to isolate. |
| Uncorrelated errors | Not reasonable in the supplied source order. The ACF shows strong positive residual autocorrelation that persists across many lags, and the time plots contain long runs above or below zero. Bookings are also clustered within two properties and common arrival dates, while the data do not identify every repeat customer. |
| Constant error variance | Not reasonable. Residual spread changes substantially across fitted ADR and forms a clear wedge/funnel pattern. |
| Normally distributed errors | Not reasonable for this preliminary model. The residual histogram is right-skewed and the QQ plot departs substantially from the reference line, especially in the upper tail. |
| No highly unusual observations | Potential unusual observations are present, including very large standardized residuals and a small high-leverage group. Source records should be checked; they should not be automatically deleted. |

Per the Part 1 instructions, this file diagnoses rather than corrects the assumption violations. Transformations, nonlinear terms, alternative variance handling, and sensitivity analyses should be considered only after the group freezes the data-cleaning decisions.
